headline: Highest risk is medium: CrewAI can write/browse with broad egress while the Spring samples are unverified and network-limited, creating plausible leakage and cascading-error paths, but no direct shared-channel evidence is present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and parse tool outputs, so a manual file bridge could carry malicious instructions into its crew. spring-integration-samples has no shared channel or writable surface documented, so the pairwise injection path is indirect and requires unusual operator bridging.
conditions: IF the operator copies B-generated text into a file that CrewAI reads as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or clipboard, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate directories.
Disable copy-paste of agent outputs into CrewAI inputs.
Add a human review step before CrewAI consumes any file from B.
Run CrewAI in a container with a read-only mount for shared inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data, API keys, and the host working directory, while spring-integration-samples is docs-only and network-limited. If they share a workspace, CrewAI can expose sensitive inputs through its broad egress; B does not show a compensating isolation mechanism, so leakage is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents access the same host directory, CrewAI can read and transmit files that B can also see.
IF developer-passed crew data includes secrets, CrewAI may leak them through model-provider calls or tool integrations.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Remove secrets from any shared input directory.
Set CrewAI to use redacted test data only.
Block outbound network for CrewAI during evaluation.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has write_filesystem and broad network_egress, while spring-integration-samples is not runnable and exposes no write capability. There is no documented locking or shared mutable resource, so direct write-write conflict is not proven; however, if both are orchestrated over the same workspace, CrewAI can overwrite artifacts B expects to remain stable.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, CrewAI can clobber files B relies on.
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents mutable access to the same resource, conflicts become likely.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Make B read-only.
Snapshot the workspace before running CrewAI.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate and act on tool outputs, and spring-integration-samples is a sample repository with no verification controls shown. If B consumes CrewAI output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports; the pair lacks a documented verification gate, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF B treats CrewAI output as ground truth without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF CrewAI is allowed to trigger tools based on its own generated content, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require human review of CrewAI outputs before B uses them.
Add a validation step that checks facts against source data.
Disable automatic action-taking from generated text.
Log and diff all inter-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for exchanged messages.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while spring-integration-samples has no data classes or residency/compliance claims documented. No concrete residency or certification mismatch is evidenced, so only a low compliance concern remains from the possibility of mishandling sensitive inputs in CrewAI.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into CrewAI inputs, compliance obligations may apply.
IF B is used to store or relay the same regulated data class, policy mismatch becomes relevant.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared test runs.
Use synthetic data for both agents.
Document retention and deletion expectations.
Review whether any secrets are passed to CrewAI.
requires-engineering: add data-class tagging and policy enforcement.
